meta.disclaimer: Tipping is discretionary everywhere in the region. Amounts below are per-guest planning guidance for independent travellers — not mandatory fees. Confirm current lodge tip sheets on arrival.

sources.label: Kafunta Safaris — Zambia walking safari scouts
Travel Currency Guide — regional money & tips

intro: Safari and lodge culture runs on cash tips for guides, trackers, scouts, and camp staff. Amounts below are per guest unless noted. Tip once at the end of each camp stay — not after every activity. Carry clean USD or local notes in small denominations; many countries reject worn USD bills. ZAR, NAD, LSL, and SZL are pegged or interchangeable with rand in their home countries — but emalangeni and maloti cannot be spent in South Africa. Ask each lodge for its tipping sheet; tip-box policies vary.

roles.guidance: USD 10–20 per guest per day (ZAR/NAD equivalent in SA/Namibia) — hand directly at checkout
USD 5–10 per guest per day — direct, often excluded from tip box
USD 5–10 per guest per day — DNPW government staff, not in lodge tip box
USD 5–15 per guest per day into communal tip box
ZAR/NAD 10–20 when they fill, check oil, and clean windscreen
USD 1–2 per bag — agree before carrying
USD 5–10 per guest per day — tip directly, not via tip box

countries.name: South Africa
countries.currency: ZAR strongly preferred; USD accepted at some tourist lodges (staff may lose on exchange)
countries.notes: Full-service petrol attendants expect ZAR 5–20. Car guards in parking lots ZAR 5–10 on return. Many Kruger/private lodges publish tip envelopes at checkout.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.currency: NAD or ZAR (1:1 peg); USD at remote lodges
countries.notes: Desert and Skeleton Coast camps often cash-only. Car guards ~NAD 10. Tip each camp separately on multi-stop routes. Etosha/Sossusvlei guides usually tipped direct.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.currency: USD preferred at Okavango/Chobe camps; BWP in Maun/Gaborone
countries.safariGuide: USD 10–20/guest/day group guide; USD 20–40 private guide — direct
countries.notes: Tip mokoro polers and trackers directly (USD 5–10/guest/day). Delta camps are often cashless for purchases — bring USD for tips. Luxury camps issue checkout guideline sheets.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.currency: USD cash in small, clean notes (post-2006); kwacha for urban small tips
countries.notes: Walking safaris: lodge guide plus armed DNPW scout — scout is NOT in tip box; tip scout USD 5–10/guest/day direct. No ATMs inside South Luangwa, Lower Zambezi, or Kafue. Victoria Falls activity guides USD 5–10 per activity.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.currency: USD cash essential (clean, post-2013 notes); ZiG change common in Vic Falls
countries.notes: Worn or marked USD bills often rejected. Withdraw or bring cash before Hwange, Mana Pools, or Matusadona — remote camps card-only for bills, not tips. Victoria Falls activity guides USD 5–10 per activity.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.currency: MZN preferred for local tips; USD at upscale beach and Gorongosa bush lodges
countries.safariGuide: USD 10–15/guest/day bush lodges; MZN 300–500/day local day guides
countries.notes: Coastal focus: Tofo/Vilankulo dive and boat crews MZN 200–500 or USD 5–10 per dive day. Withdraw meticais before Bazaruto/Quirimbas islands. Gorongosa is main bush-safari tipping context.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.currency: USD for lodge and safari tips; MWK for porters and markets
countries.notes: Lake Malawi kayak/skippers USD 3–5 or small MWK per outing. Clean USD notes required. Few ATMs outside Lilongwe and Blantyre — carry USD for lake lodges and parks.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.currency: LSL/ZAR interchangeably (1:1); cash essential in highlands
countries.notes: Malealea and similar operators suggest ~ZAR 30–40/group/day for pony guides (tip direct, not on lodge invoice). Sani Pass and highland villages are card-free — bring rand/maloti in small notes.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.currency: SZL/ZAR interchangeably (1:1); spend emalangeni before exiting to SA
countries.notes: Mantenga and cultural village guides ZAR/SZL 50–100 per visit or performance. Big Game Parks lodges usually have communal tip boxes. USD accepted at tourist lodges but rand is simpler.
